candidates.title: The man who phoned in Canada's most famous UFO sighting became the face of the mystery
candidates.description: The Oct. 4, 1967, Shag Harbour event is considered Canada's most famous UFO incident. Laurie Wickens became the public face of the mystery, a role he kept until his recent death at 76.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lurkers in the deep: How Canada's new submarines will be used in peace and potential war
candidates.description: The Canadian government has often spoken about the need for submarines to patrol Canada's vast coastline. But the role and range of of its new submarines go far beyond merely patrolling the three coasts of the country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Evacuations underway as fast-growing wildfires threaten communities in B.C.'s Interior
candidates.description: Evacuations are underway around two fast-growing wildfires in B.C.’s Interior, one near the Okanagan Lake and another in the East Kootenay.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Montreal police investigating suspicious fire at kosher restaurant
candidates.description: Police are investigating a suspicious fire that broke out overnight at a kosher restaurant in Montreal's Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce borough.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Pimicikamak Cree Nation under lockdown after gunshots fired, 1 person dead: chief
candidates.description: Pimicikamak Cree Nation Chief David Monias says a shooter is still on the loose and the northern Manitoba remains in lockdown Saturday morning after gunshots were fired and one person died.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The mystery of the 'Great Wall' of Hant’s Harbour
candidates.description: Though the local nickname “The Great Wall” may be tongue-in-cheek, it does reflect the intensive labour that must have gone into building these structures.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How a road trip detour to Tumbler Ridge led this tourist from Taiwan to a 100-million-year-old dinosaur track
candidates.description: One of five UNESCO Geoparks in Canada, Tumbler Ridge has been attracting people from around the world who are helping to uncover the region's dinosaur past.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Aboriginal to Indigenous: Leaders, advocates reflect on decades of state linguistic changes
candidates.description: Ten years after the Government of Canada officially adopted the term "Indigenous" instead of "Aboriginal," discussions persist on what terms best describe First Nations, Inuit and Métis.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Convicted drug trafficker to keep Halifax-area lakeside home, but will pay $240K fine
candidates.description: Gary (Boo) Boudreau, who was targeted by a major cocaine and cannabis investigation, will not lose the million-dollar lakeside home he built partly on the proceeds of crime, but has instead been ordered to pay a $240,000 fine for the portion linked to his illegal profits.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadians ready to play ball as 1st season of Women's Pro Baseball League gets underway
candidates.description: Nearly a dozen Canadian athletes are going to be part of the chase to be the first-ever champions of the Women's Pro Baseball League, which begins its inaugural season in the United States on Saturday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 2 teens charged with 2nd-degree murder of woman in Prince Albert, Sask.
candidates.description: Two teenagers have been charged with second-degree murder after 27-year-old Daina Gauthier was fatally stabbed on Thursday in Prince Albert.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: One of Calgary's most decorated Second World War veterans dies at 101
candidates.description: Navy Capt. William (Bill) Wilson enlisted in the Royal Canadian Navy in 1942, serving aboard HMCS Ottawa as a seaman gunner during the latter stages of the Battle of the Atlantic and taking part in the D-Day landings at Normandy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Kayaker on St. John River makes a pair of grim discoveries
candidates.description: ​Melissa Lavigne has done a lot of kayaking on the St. John River, but on a recent paddle, she came across something new: a headstone and grave marker for two long-dead Fredericton men.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Winnipeg man pleads guilty to advocating genocide and wilfully promoting hatred in social media posts
candidates.description: A Winnipeg man who self-identified as being "extremely racist" in posts he made on social media has pleaded guilty to advocating genocide and wilfully promoting hatred against Muslims and Jews.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Saskatoon fire crews searching river after reports of missing person, dog
candidates.description: Reports of a person and dog in the river came in at 11:50 a.m. CST on Friday, said Saskatoon fire chief Doug Wegren.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: On Ukraine's front lines, female soldiers testing Canadian-designed body armour
candidates.description: Ukrainian soldiers on the front lines of Russia's war are testing new body armour designed by a Canadian company to fit women so that they no longer have to wear ill-fitting ballistic plates made for men.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hunger and hostility cited by migrants as reason for return to Morocco from Spain's Ceuta
candidates.description: Ceuta migration influx has resulted in tens of thousands of migrants who originally travelled into the Spanish territory to return to North Africa; Spain to put up containment fence.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Bombing near upscale Moscow restaurant kills 3 people, wounds at least 21
candidates.description: Russian state media, citing local authorities, reported an unidentified woman carrying a homemade bomb tried to get into an upscale restaurant in central Moscow but was stopped by a security guard.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nirmal Purja, 'inspirational' Nepali climber, among 10 killed in avalanche during Pakistan expedition
candidates.description: Purja, 43, and nine others had been missing since Thursday after being struck by an avalanche on Broad Peak, the world's 12th-highest ​mountain, in Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan region.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What French communities have learned after a week of battling wildfires that threaten their way of life
candidates.description: People in communities across southwestern France have spent the last week volunteering to aid firefighting efforts as blazes ravage the pine forests near their small towns. Now they face a difficult transition as they move from crisis response to figuring out how to prevent the fires threatening their entire way of life.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Authorities release Nancy Guthrie ransom note in search for new leads | Hanomansing Tonight
candidates.description: Investigators have released the full ransom note and a follow-up letter tied to the disappearance of Today Show host Savannah Guthrie's mom, who was abducted from her home in Arizona six months ago. Authorities are looking to the public in hopes the writing style in the notes will help generate new leads in the investigation.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What is Ceuta, and how was the Spanish enclave near Morocco breached by 60,000 migrants?
candidates.description: Current estimates are some 60,000 people crossed into the Spanish enclave in North Africa on Thursday — and by Friday, that an estimated 48,300 had returned to Morocco. Here's what we know.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. Justice Department dismisses case against ex-Olympian accused of damaging D.C. reflecting pool
candidates.description: The U.S. Justice Department moved Friday to dismiss a criminal case charging a former Olympian with deliberately damaging the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada, allies express renewed concern over North Korean IT worker scheme
candidates.description: North Korea has continuously deployed a network of remote IT workers to defraud businesses and transfer revenues toward the proliferation of nuclear weapons, says a statement by Global Affairs Canada and its counterparts in nine other countries.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: First 7-Eleven, now Zabka: Canadian convenience giant Alimentation Couche-Tard eyes takeover of Polish rival
candidates.description: The Laval, Que.-based owner of Couche-Tard and Circle K stores announced Friday that it made an offer valued at more than $12 billion to buy Polish convenience store operator Zabka Group. The play comes after Alimentation Couche-Tard tried, but failed, to buy the parent company of 7-Eleven for more than a year.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Two crew killed as British pilot survives after firefighting helicopters collide in Greece
candidates.description: One Danish and one Greek national died in the incident, while a British pilot and another Greek crew member survived.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump cancels Iran strikes subject to deal being made 'rapidly'
candidates.description: The US president claims Iran and other Middle Eastern countries asked Washington to hold off on any attack as the "perimeters" of a deal had been agreed.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: At least 13 killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza after Hamas agree disarmament deal
candidates.description: Israel says it was targeting military operatives in the strikes on Gaza City, Khan Younis and Deir el-Balah.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How Spain's migrant crisis created a political storm - whipped up by social media
candidates.description: The Ceuta crossings have shaken Europe politically, exposing divisions over the sensitive issue of migration, the BBC's Sarah Rainsford writes.

candidates.title: Young guns for hire - the teenage hitmen recruited to kill across Europe

candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Uganda unveils statue of Israel PM's brother who died in Entebbe rescue mission
candidates.description: Yonatan Netanyahu was the only Israeli soldier to die as he led a mission to free more than 100 hostages.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Tourist plane crashes in Peru, killing 13
candidates.description: The small plane was flying over the Nazca Lines ​archaeological site when it crashed, according to local reports.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Italy putting nearly all major cities on highest heat alert
candidates.description: Some 19 major Italian cities - including Rome, Milan and Naples - are already on red alert, and by Monday all but two will be.

candidates.title: Three killed after bomb detonated at Moscow restaurant, state media say
candidates.description: Security officials said a woman tried to enter the restaurant with explosives but was stopped by a security guard.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Body of mountaineer Nirmal Purja recovered after Pakistan avalanche
candidates.description: The renowned climber was known for scaling the world's 14 highest peaks in just over six months in 2019.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: A bruising 24 hours - what next for Fifa and under-pressure Infantino?
candidates.description: Pressure is building on Gianni Infantino. Can he survive as Fifa president after the implosion of the controversial World Cup investment plan?

candidates.title: Solitude as a new aspirational lifestyle: 'We are not lonely'
candidates.description: A growing number of so-called "loneliness influencers" are spotlighting solo living without children or friends - and it's spurring debate.

candidates.title: Ginger hair portraits show unexpected 'golden thread' connecting Americans
candidates.description: For Kieran Dodds, photographing people with red hair has become something of an obsession over the past decade or more.

candidates.title: Infantino on the brink? Who might replace him if he goes?
candidates.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino is in the eye of a storm after scrapping his attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup. If he goes, who comes in?

candidates.title: At the scene of deadly Moscow bomb blast
candidates.description: Three people have been killed and 21 injured after an explosive device detonated at an Italian restaurant, Russian media reports.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Fastest runner to cross the Alps says it was an incredible experience

candidates.title: Crowds line Amsterdam's canals for Pride boat parade
candidates.description: Costumed participants danced and waved from a colourful flotilla of 80 decorated vessels as they made their way through the city's waterways.

candidates.title: Scientist's lifelong obsession with mystery of elusive 'pink zebra' seaweed

candidates.title: Injured peregrine reunion 'brought tears to eyes'

candidates.title: Should you take the plunge? How to tell how clean the sea is

candidates.title: Breakfasts around the world: In Australia, being denied vegemite is grounds for suing

candidates.title: Trump says he's cancelling Iran strikes, deal pending
candidates.description: Trump said Iran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked the U.S. "to hold off any attack" on Iran because "the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to."

candidates.title: Avalanche in Pakistan kills famed mountaineer Nirmal Purja and his fellow climbers

candidates.author: NPR

candidates.author: NPR

candidates.author: NPR

candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why did OpenAI's and Anthropic's AI models hack other companies?

candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: FIFA scraps controversial deal to sell stakes in World Cup to private investors
candidates.description: FIFA abandoned a plan to create a commercial venture and then sell stakes to minority investors, just days after unveiling it. The plan drew sharp condemnation — and a boycott from European nations.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Oil companies report sky-high profits thanks to wartime crude prices

candidates.author: NPR

candidates.author: NPR

candidates.description: Doctors are seeing more children injured - some badly - from e-bikes and e-scooters. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks with Dr. Cornelia Griggs and Caitlin Coit of Mass General Brigham for Children Hospital.

candidates.title: Why is the rate of premature births so high in this community?
candidates.description: About 1 in 4 babies in the Pakistani fishing settlement of Rehri Goth are born prematurely. Researchers are trying to figure out how to bring the numbers down.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What Cyclospora does inside the gut and how it gets there

candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Entomologist Stephen Dobson on releasing modified mosquitoes to fight disease

candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How these slum dwellers went from one-room shacks to beautiful new apartments
candidates.description: It's a bold new experiment and it's already won a prize. Residents in a jam-packed slum, many of them living in one-room tin shacks, help design their apartments in a brand new building.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: FDA weighs a new kind of flu shot based on technology RFK Jr. has questioned
candidates.description: The FDA is poised to render a decision on Moderna's mRNA-based flu shot, which could be the first of its kind to market. The decision is expected to reverberate throughout the biotech industry.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Nurses chase Cyclospora using grocery receipts, food apps and detailed interviews
candidates.description: Public health nurses have been pulled from other duties in Washtenaw County, MI, to call hundreds of people sick with cyclosporiasis, and try to help them remember everything they ate in recent days.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What's it like to be on the frontlines of the Cyclosporiasis outbreak?
candidates.description: What it's like on the on the frontlines of the public health investigation into cyclosporiasis, in Washtenaw County, Michigan, which just finished with a measles outbreak?
candidates.author: NPR
